The offending helper is:

- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:906-913` — `typec_partner_unlink_device()`

```c
906 static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner,
907                                         struct device *dev)
908 {
909     sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));
910     sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
911
912     if (partner->deattach)
913         partner->deattach(partner, dev);
}
```

The `"typec"` link is initially created by:

- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:888-904` — `typec_partner_link_device()`

```c
892 ret = sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &partner->dev.kobj, "typec");
```

## Why the warning says “no directory”

`sysfs_remove_link()` is implemented at:

- `fs/sysfs/symlink.c:143-153`

```c
143 void sysfs_remove_link(struct kobject *kobj, const char *name)
...
152     kernfs_remove_by_name(parent, name);
```

`parent` is derived from `kobj->sd`:

- `fs/sysfs/symlink.c:145-152`

```c
145 struct kernfs_node *parent = NULL;
...
149     parent = kobj->sd;
...
152 kernfs_remove_by_name(parent, name);
```

The warning is emitted when that `sd`/directory pointer is NULL:

- `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1724-1734`

```c
1724 int kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(struct kernfs_node *parent, ...)
...
1730 if (!parent) {
1731     WARN(1, KERN_WARNING
1732          "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n", name);
1733     return -ENOENT;
1734 }
```

Thus, `-ENOENT` here means that the parent kobject directory no longer exists. It is not primarily “the symlink was absent”; it is specifically the `"typec"` removal being attempted with no valid kernfs directory for the USB device.

The USB device can reach that state through its normal removal path:

- `drivers/base/core.c:3833-3903` — `device_del()`
- `drivers/base/core.c:3897-3900` — emits removal, deletes the kobject
- `drivers/base/core.c:3917-3922` — `device_unregister()`

```c
3897 kobject_uevent(&dev->kobj, KOBJ_REMOVE);
3899 kobject_del(&dev->kobj);
...
3917 void device_unregister(struct device *dev)
3919     device_del(dev);
```

After `kobject_del()`, `dev->kobj.sd` is no longer a usable kernfs directory. A later `sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")` therefore reaches `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(NULL, "typec", ...)` and produces exactly the reported warning.

## The second offending function: `typec_partner_deattach()`

The Type-C class also installs a detach callback:

- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:2752-2753`

```c
port->con.attach = typec_partner_attach;
port->con.deattach = typec_partner_deattach;
```

The callback is:

- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:2169-2186`

```c
2169 static void typec_partner_deattach(struct typec_connector *con,
2170                                    struct device *dev)
{
2174     mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
2175     partner = typec_get_partner(port);
2176     if (partner) {
2177         typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, dev);
2178         put_device(&partner->dev);
2179     }
...
2181     if (port->usb2_dev == dev)
2182         port->usb2_dev = NULL;
2183     else if (port->usb3_dev == dev)
2184         port->usb3_dev = NULL;
```

This is the fundamental design error:

1. `typec_unregister_partner()` explicitly calls `typec_partner_unlink_device()` at `class.c:1185`/`1189`.
2. `typec_partner_unlink_device()` invokes `partner->deattach()` at `class.c:912`.
3. The installed callback is `typec_partner_deattach()`.
4. `typec_partner_deattach()` calls `typec_partner_unlink_device()` again at `class.c:2177`.

Therefore the same relationship is removed through both the explicit partner-unregister path and the detach callback path. Depending on device-removal ordering, the second removal may see either:

- an already-removed symlink, yielding ordinary `-ENOENT`, or
- a kobject whose kernfs directory has already been deleted, yielding the visible `"no directory"` warning.

The exact Type-C functions involved are therefore:

- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:888` — `typec_partner_link_device()`
- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:906` — `typec_partner_unlink_device()`
- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1174` — `typec_unregister_partner()`
- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:2144` — `typec_partner_attach()`
- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:2169` — `typec_partner_deattach()`

and the UCSI functions are:

- `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1138` — `ucsi_unregister_partner()`
- `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1201` — `ucsi_check_connection()`
- `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1264` — `ucsi_handle_connector_change()`

## Is the fix already in this tree?

No. The indexed tree still contains the unfixed combination:

```text
typec_unregister_partner()
  -> typec_partner_unlink_device()
       -> partner->deattach()
            -> typec_partner_unlink_device()
```

In particular, it still has:

- `class.c:912` calling `partner->deattach()` from the generic unlink helper;
- `class.c:1185` and `1189` calling that helper during partner destruction;
- `class.c:2177` recursively calling the same helper from `typec_partner_deattach()`.

That is the offending implementation.

## Upstream fix

The upstream fix is the Type-C class change that **separates link removal from detach notification**. The unlink operation used while destroying a partner must not invoke the connector's `deattach` callback; the callback is intended for a device disappearing while the partner remains alive.

Equivalently, the fix changes the partner-link removal path so that partner destruction performs only:

```text
remove partner-side symlink
remove device-side "typec" symlink
```

and does **not** call `typec_partner_deattach()` from that path. Detach notification remains on the actual device-detach path.

This fix is commonly described in the upstream Type-C patch series as the fix for **double removal of Type-C partner links / partner deattach handling**. It is not present in the supplied tree; the Dell warning is therefore expected on kernels based on this pre-fix implementation.

The minimal conceptual correction is one of:

```c
typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, dev, bool notify);
```

with partner destruction passing `false`, or splitting the helper into separate “remove links” and “detach device” functions. Simply suppressing the kernfs warning would mask the bug rather than fix the invalid second unlink.
